# QS-CFW-7855-84 - Quality specification - valve body CFW-7855-84 (F316)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-7855-84

Scope
This document defines quality acceptance criteria and inspection methods for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) manufactured from F316 forgings at Plant P1. It applies to finished forgings released for machining and assembly.

Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Hardness | The hardness range for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 32-36 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is ±0.05 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 105.0 kg. |

Inspection method
- Hardness: Perform hardness testing on finished forgings at locations representative of the bore and web. Use a calibrated hardness tester and follow manufacturer's procedure for HRC scale. Record each measured value and compare to the hardness range shown in the requirements table.
- Bore diameter: Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauge or coordinate measuring equipment. Verify final machined bore complies with the bore diameter tolerance stated in the requirements table. Record measured dimensions on the inspection record.
- Weight: Verify forging weight by scale check after final forging cooling and prior to shipment or transfer to machining. Compare measured mass to the maximum forging weight in the requirements table. Include weight entry on the lot inspection report.

Nonconformance handling
- Any item failing to meet the specified hardness, bore tolerance, or maximum forging weight shall be segregated and labeled as nonconforming. Notify quality engineering and document the condition on the lot nonconformance record.
- Disposition options include authorized rework or scrap as determined by quality engineering and production leadership. Reworked parts must be reinspected to the same specified requirements prior to release.
- All nonconformance actions and final dispositions shall be recorded and retained in the document control system according to company retention practice.
